DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.842.setting: Chorley Mental Health Inpatient Unit, Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust (psychiatric inpatient wards)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.842.standard: 20-item list of expected clerking components based on trust guidelines

cycle1.result: Highest completion: clerking within 6 hours, consultant face-to-face review within a week and current medication documentation. Lowest completion: clinical impression, bloods within 24 hours, capacity assessment and smoking/substance history (no percentages given).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.842.intervention: Planned: standardised capacity assessment documentation and a clerking checklist; results presented at local teaching and recommendations sent to Site Tutors for local inductions.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.842.other_findings: Poorer clerkings were linked to poor patient engagement and transfer from another ward. A survey of 8 trainees found no uniform method for capacity documentation and no official clerking checklist.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.412.setting: Psychiatric Liaison Service, Queen's Hospital (NELFT), older adults over 65

cycle1.result: 47% of older adult referrals to PLS had delirium; 87% of delirium referrals needed no further PLS intervention after initial assessment; 31 delirium referrals to the Dementia and Delirium Team.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.412.intervention: Simplified PLS referral form with a mandatory 4AT delirium score and mandatory referral to the Dementia and Delirium Team for positive screens (November 2023).

cycle2.result: 35% of referrals had delirium; 58% of delirium referrals needed no further PLS intervention; prior screening and referral to Dementia and Delirium Team rose by 4%; 85 delirium referrals to the Dementia and Delirium Team (174% increase).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.412.other_findings: This is the first stage of a multi-phase quality improvement and service development project.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.853.setting: Inner city community mental health team (CMHT) outpatient clinics
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.853.standard: Trust protocol: clinics cancelled only when absolutely necessary and patients informed at least 8 weeks before the appointed clinic

cycle1.result: About 54% of 193 booked clinics were cancelled (68% in September, 30.30% in August). Around 50% of patients were informed 8 weeks in advance. Causes: junior doctor on call 31.58%, annual leave 25%, study leave 21%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.853.other_findings: 72% of cancellations were by junior doctors and 28% by consultants; poor communication between clinicians and the appointment booking team was the main cause.

DOI:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2025.1619.setting: North Tyneside Community Treatment Team, Cumbria, Northumberland, Tyne and Wear Trust
DOI:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2025.1619.standard: NICE and local trust guidelines: 100% of patients on depot antipsychotics have a GASS form yearly; 100% have a GASS ever; completed GASS forms accessible on RiO

cycle1.result: 88% had a GASS in the past year; 97% of GASS recorded on RiO.

cycle2.result: 53% had a GASS completed in the past year (red); 95% had a GASS ever (green); 98% of GASS recorded on RiO (green).

DOI:10.1192/j.eurpsy.2025.1619.other_findings: This was the fourth re-audit; the fall in yearly GASS completion was attributed to COVID-19 disruption of face-to-face reviews. Re-audit planned for 2024/25.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.545.setting: Beechcroft, step 5 regional child and adolescent mental health inpatient unit, Belfast
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.545.standard: 7 criteria of necessary referral information (identifiers, referrer, location, legal status, presenting symptoms, working diagnosis, risks warranting admission)

cycle1.result: Overall 75.2% of criteria met. Identifiers and referrer 100%, presenting symptoms 95%, risks 79%, legal status 74%, location 68%, working diagnosis 11% (2/19).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.545.intervention: Planned: in-hours bed manager appointed and a standardised referral proforma to be developed; re-audit planned.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.545.other_findings: Working diagnosis was missing in 90% of referrals and risks or legal status missing in up to a quarter.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.345.setting: Mental Health Liaison Team, Hertfordshire Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.345.standard: Project aim: handover time under 30 minutes within one month and improved handover quality

cycle1.result: Average handover 44 minutes; 7 interruptions; key information available 69%; staff member allocated 80%; review date allocated 83%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.345.intervention: Two PDSA cycles guided by human factors analysis (driver diagram and change ideas), avoiding a rigid handover system; specific changes not detailed.

cycle2.result: Average handover 30 minutes; 2 interruptions; key information 92%; staff member allocated 95%; review date allocated 95%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.345.other_findings: Average patients discussed per handover unchanged (15). Burnout, understaffing and COVID-19 were key human factors; re-audit planned at 6 and 12 months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10549.setting: Three older adult psychiatric inpatient wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10549.standard: Trust Record Management Policy: 80% of entries validated, within 12 hours; GMC Good Medical Practice

cycle1.result: not reported

cycle2.result: Validated entries improved on all three wards (up to 35% increase on one ward) but overall validation remained below the 80% standard; most validated entries met the 12-hour standard.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10549.other_findings: Doctors were more likely to validate entries in normal working hours than out of hours. The cycle led to a wider QI project and trustwide policy change on validation.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab430.067.topic: Timing of cholecystectomy after acute biliary admission
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab430.067.setting: Central London tertiary care centre (Guy's and St Thomas' Hospital)
DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab430.067.standard: AUGIS: laparoscopic cholecystectomy on index admission for acute cholecystitis and gallstone pancreatitis, ideally within 72 hours

cycle1.result: Average waiting time to laparoscopic cholecystectomy 98.2 weeks.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab430.067.intervention: Dedicated e-referral system for patients who did not have cholecystectomy on index admission.

cycle2.result: Average waiting time to laparoscopic cholecystectomy 47.7 weeks.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znab430.067.other_findings: Readmissions fell by 23.3% in choledocholithiasis, 17.4% biliary colic, 16.7% ascending cholangitis, 12.8% acute cholecystitis and 8.3% gallstone pancreatitis. 243 patients in total across both years.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.456.topic: Dementia diagnostic assessment and post-diagnostic care
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.456.setting: Community Mental Health Services for Older People, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.456.standard: NICE 2018 dementia guideline and TEWV 2019 person-centred dementia care pathway

cycle1.result: Consent recorded 80%; prognosis information 47%; dementia and driving information 26%; accessible information leaflets 16%; carer's assessment offered 26%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.456.intervention: Action plans on areas needing improvement (not detailed).

cycle2.result: Consent recorded 65%; prognosis information 80%; dementia and driving 53%; accessible leaflets 50%; carer's assessment offered 18%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.456.other_findings: Carer's assessment stayed below standard in both cycles and consent recording fell. COVID-19 lockdown was thought to have limited leaflet sharing.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.36.setting: All wards of a children's hospital (medical and critical care)
DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.36.standard: Local guidelines, 100%: all patients on oxygen have a prescription, target saturations, administration device and nurse signature within last 12 hours

cycle1.result: 0/14 had an oxygen prescription (13 patients receiving oxygen reported).

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.36.intervention: New paediatric medication chart with an oxygen prescription section and a training package for doctors, nurses and pharmacists; awareness of initial audit results.

cycle2.result: 4/18 had an oxygen prescription (22%), all medical patients; of these target saturations 100%, device 25%, nurse signature within 12 hours 100%.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.36.other_findings: No prescribing in critical care (14 patients), which had not engaged with the new chart.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.036.setting: Oesophago-Gastric Anastomosis Audit: 137 hospitals in 41 countries (prospective multicentre cohort)

cycle1.result: Anastomotic leak rate 14.2% (n = 319) and conduit necrosis rate 2.7% (n = 60). CN risk score (BMI, ECOG, previous MI, smoking) validated with AUROC 0.775; AL score AUROC 0.618.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac404.036.other_findings: Anastomotic leak was difficult to predict from preoperative factors; external validation of the CN score is needed.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.210.setting: Tertiary cancer units, secondary care and community services (National Oesophagogastric Nutrition Audit survey)

cycle1.result: 77% of tertiary surgical units felt able to provide adequate post-operative nutritional care; 52% (diagnostic phase) and 67% (neoadjuvant period) disagreed they could provide adequate dietetic support.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znad348.210.other_findings: Barriers were inadequate funding, understaffing and prioritisation of inpatients; wide variation in service structure and staffing.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.511.standard: MDT-agreed standard for daily progress notes: clear language and information on mental state, medication, meals, physical health, personal care, activities, risks and use of leave

cycle1.result: Accessibility of information scored 1 on average (Likert +3 to -3); language scored 2; personal care information present in 17%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.511.intervention: Standards and a suggested note format emailed to staff, with follow-up meetings with individual staff and the MDT to resolve difficulties.

cycle2.result: Accessibility 3 on average; language 2; all content items increased; meals, medication and physical health present 100%; personal care 89%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.511.other_findings: Largest improvement was in personal care information (17% to 89%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10695.setting: Community Learning Disability Team psychiatry caseload, London
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10695.standard: Established criteria for genetic testing in unexplained moderate, severe or profound intellectual disability

cycle1.result: 39 had moderate to profound ID; 20.5% had a confirmed genetic diagnosis; genetic testing mentioned in 25.6% of those with moderate or severe ID; only one patient referred for testing by this team.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10695.intervention: Planned: targeted education for the team, sharing the Clinical Genetics referral protocol and a prompt in initial assessments.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10695.other_findings: Most previous genetic referrals were made under paediatric or child learning disability services.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11723.setting: Adult mental health male and female acute inpatient wards, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11723.standard: TEWV trust policy on regular review of anxiolytics and hypnotics

cycle1.result: Inpatient prescriptions reviewed and documented: 26% (female, 100 prescriptions) and 46% (male, 35); reviewed weekly 6% (female) and 0% (male). Documented discharge plan for benzodiazepine/z-drug review 74% (female) and 91% (male).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11723.other_findings: Most prescriptions were reviewed only at discharge (71% female and 22% male discharge prescriptions changed). Weekly MDT reviews and training for doctors in training recommended.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.532.setting: Two general adult Community Mental Health Teams (Recovery Team)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.532.standard: NICE and Maudsley guidelines: annual FBC, U&E, eGFR, lipids, LFT, HbA1c/glucose and prolactin where required; compliance 80% or above recommended

cycle1.result: U&E 77%, glucose/HbA1c 74%, FBC and LFT ~72% (76 patients), eGFR 60%, prolactin 31% (9 patients); all below 80%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.532.intervention: Recommendations to existing monitoring services and liaison to set up a dedicated physical health clinic (recruitment under way); re-audit planned.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.532.other_findings: 66% of blood tests were done in GP surgeries and 25% by mental health services.

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2019-nppc.24.standard: Local Multidisciplinary Guidelines for Acute Pain Management in Children and Young People: all patients on opioids have PRN naloxone with correct directions

cycle1.result: Naloxone prescribed in 17% (7/41); on PRN section 100% (7/7); correct directions 86% (6/7).

DOI:10.1136/archdischild-2019-nppc.24.intervention: Planned: presentation at paediatric and surgical paediatric audit meetings to educate prescribers.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.529.setting: Enfield South Locality Team, Barnet, Enfield and Haringey Mental Health Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.529.standard: Team-agreed audit standards (95%) on monitoring frequency, time to review and need for referral

cycle1.result: Only 7/30 (23.33%) tested within the last year; 2 (6.667%) new hyperprolactinaemia diagnoses, both reviewed and treated within one month. No audit standards were met.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.529.intervention: New risk-stratified hyperprolactinaemia guidance developed; re-audit planned for 2020.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.529.other_findings: Reasons for failure included loss to follow-up, tests not requested and missed appointments.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10648.topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10648.setting: Cedar Ward adult mental health admissions ward, Llandough Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10648.standard: NCEPOD 2022 report on physical health care in mental health inpatients

cycle1.result: Physical health plan 100%; bloods 72%; physical examination 79%; ECG 70%; urine dip 15%; nervous system examination 43%; 17% had physical health conditions not updated on PARIS.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10648.intervention: Planned: standard proforma for physical health assessment.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10648.other_findings: Lack of uniform documentation made data collection difficult; SHOs were the first point of contact for physical health assessment.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11736.setting: Inpatient alcohol detox unit, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust, East Midlands

cycle1.result: Preparatory work information missing in 72.73% (16/22); written plans 68.18% (15/22); relapse prevention medication mentioned 81.82%; psychological support 59.09%; mental health mentioned 86.36%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11736.intervention: Referral form refined to capture preparatory work and prompt consideration of mental health support.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11736.other_findings: 86.36% were out-of-area referrals; 68.42% of those with mental health mentioned had no plan to refer to a local mental health team.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11829.setting: Liaison Psychiatry service, Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11829.standard: NICE guidance and local trust policies: 100% documentation of sexual dysfunction presence/absence and/or advice on sexual side effects at medication initiation

cycle1.result: Consent for psychotropic initiation documented in 64%; sexual side-effect discussion documented in 4%; other side effects discussed in 19%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11829.intervention: Planned: clear documentation and education; re-audit within 8 months.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11829.other_findings: 97 of 1214 patients assessed were started on psychotropic medication.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.588.topic: Buccal midazolam prescribing and carer training in epilepsy
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.588.setting: Intellectual disability services, Hertfordshire and Essex mental health services
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.588.standard: ESNA and ILAE national guidelines for PRN buccal midazolam administration

cycle1.result: not reported

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.588.other_findings: Data collection was still under way at the time of the abstract; no results reported.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.578.setting: Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust (POMH lithium audit participation)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.578.standard: NICE guidelines: six-monthly TFTs, calcium, eGFR and serum lithium in maintenance; weight/BMI/waist circumference within 12 months; compared with POMH national performance

cycle1.result: Six-monthly calcium 64%, TFTs 78%, eGFR 83%, serum lithium 87%; weight/BMI/waist within 12 months 71%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.578.intervention: Planned: Quality Performance Alert to medical and nursing staff and lithium monitoring added to junior doctor induction.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.578.other_findings: TFT and weight/BMI monitoring were above the POMH national level; serum lithium, eGFR and calcium were below it.

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.025.topic: Steroid-induced hyperglycaemia screening in giant cell arteritis
DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.025.standard: British Society for Rheumatology GCA guideline: HbA1c monitoring and documented counselling on steroid-induced hyperglycaemia

cycle1.result: Baseline HbA1c checked in 32/60 (53%); counselling documented 7/60 (12%); hyperglycaemia detected 8/60 (13%).

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.025.intervention: Results presented at a regional meeting to raise awareness and a GCA clinic was set up.

cycle2.result: Baseline HbA1c checked in 28/30 (93%); counselling documented 9/30 (30%); hyperglycaemia detected 11/30 (36%).

DOI:10.1093/rheumatology/keac133.025.other_findings: Those developing hyperglycaemia had higher baseline weight and BMI. Counselling remained poor and was the priority for further work.

DOI:10.1002/bjs.9883.topic: Core outcome set for breast reconstruction
DOI:10.1002/bjs.9883.setting: BRAVO study, Delphi survey of patients and professionals

cycle1.result: 303 (51.4 per cent) completed round 1 and 259 (85.5 per cent) round 2; 148 items in 34 domains led to a core outcome set of 11 key outcomes.

DOI:10.1002/bjs.9883.other_findings: Consensus methodology study, not an audit.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.231.topic: Physical assessment of mental health patients in the emergency department
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.231.setting: Bolton A&E referrals to the Bolton Mental Health Liaison Team
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.231.standard: Royal College of Emergency Medicine guidelines on physical assessment before mental health referral

cycle1.result: 44% had any physical observations; 37% had full physical assessment before referral; 58% of abnormal observations were acted on.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.231.intervention: Recommended: joint guidelines and teaching for A&E and MHLT practitioners.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.231.other_findings: 2% near-miss rate, including a missed diabetic ketoacidosis and delayed treatment of a missed overdose; some triage notes said only "mental health".

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.440.setting: Acute female psychiatric inpatient ward, Greater Manchester Mental Health Trust

cycle1.result: 7/15 (47%) had a documented urine pregnancy test on admission; of 8 untested, only 1 had contraceptive use documented and 7 had no LMP/contraception notes.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.440.intervention: Recommended nursing admission checklist recording LMP, contraception and recent unprotected sex when urine is refused; re-audit planned January to June 2022.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.440.other_findings: Pregnancy test strips were unavailable on the ward for about a month; one untested patient was later found to be pregnant.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.573.setting: Amber Ward (old age dementia ward), Millbrook Mental Health Unit, Nottinghamshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.573.standard: 10 standards from the Maudsley Prescribing Guidelines covert medication pathway

cycle1.result: LPA/best interest discussion 85% (n = 12); pharmacy input 47% (n = 7); administration in drug chart 53% (n = 8); review date 67% (n = 10); MDT discussion 100% (n = 15).

cycle2.dates: Service users initiated January 2021 to June 2022
cycle2.result: LPA/best interest discussion 95% (n = 20); pharmacy input 100% (n = 21); drug chart administration 100% (n = 21); review date 85% (n = 18); MDT discussion 90% (n = 19); 100% compliance in 4 of 10 standards.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.573.other_findings: MDT discussion documentation fell; strict use of the existing covert medication initiation form and another re-audit within 2 years recommended.

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.478.topic: Skin cancer education in organ transplant recipients
DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.478.setting: Two national transplant centres (inpatient wards, outpatient dermatology and transplant clinics), London

cycle1.result: Prior skin cancer education 66% (site A) and 78% (site B); awareness of increased risk 89% (A) and 95% (B); knowledge of monthly self-examination 28% (A) and 49% (B).

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.478.intervention: Educational poster displayed clinically and distributed online.

cycle2.result: Awareness of increased risk 96% (A) and 100% (B); sun protection confidence 89% (A) and 96% (B); monthly self-examination knowledge 77% (A) and 81% (B); confidence performing skin checks 79% (A) and 86% (B).

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljag086.478.other_findings: At site A awareness of seeking GP review for suspected skin cancer rose from 47% to 92% and vitamin D advice from 57% to 94%. 158 responses in total (site A 47, site B 111).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11726.topic: Blood test rationale for memantine and pregabalin
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11726.setting: Older People's Mental Health inpatient unit
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11726.standard: NICE and BNF (no routine blood monitoring for memantine or pregabalin), RCPath renal testing advice and NHS England guidance that all blood tests have a documented rationale

cycle1.result: 92 blood tests in 30 patients; rationale documented for 62% (n=37); renal monitoring for psychotropics was the rationale in 42% (n=24) of these, all with previously normal kidney function.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11726.intervention: Recommended: MDT discussion of monitoring rationale and clear documentation for all blood tests.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11726.other_findings: 25% (n=23) of tests without rationale may have related to memantine or pregabalin initiation or titration.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.216.setting: Torfaen area community services and Talygarn ward, Aneurin Bevan University Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.216.standard: BNF: prolactin at baseline, after 6 months and then annually

cycle1.result: 23 of 28 on risperidone/paliperidone never had prolactin measured; 2 of 28 had appropriate monitoring for 2018.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.216.intervention: Awareness of baseline prolactin monitoring raised and baseline prolactin added to admission bloods for patients with psychosis or on antipsychotics.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.216.other_findings: 150 patients' letters were screened to find 28 on the medications.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11295.setting: Three acute psychiatric inpatient units (Wrexham, Rhyl and Bangor), Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11295.standard: 60 essential criteria derived from the Oxford Textbook of Psychiatry on history taking and mental state examination; 100% target

cycle1.result: Aggregate compliance 50.6%; administrative tasks 84.3%; objective MSE 68.5%; HOPC 26.4%; past psychiatric history 22.9%; risk assessment 58.1% but risk management plan 8.6%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11295.intervention: Planned: training sessions for trainee doctors before re-audit.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11295.other_findings: Different clerking proformas were used at the three sites; anxiety symptoms documented in 10.0% and depression in 26.8%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11834.topic: Tissue box availability in clinic rooms
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11834.setting: Three community outpatient psychiatric bases, Hertfordshire Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11834.standard: Consensually agreed gold standard of 100% tissue box availability in all clinic rooms

cycle1.result: Location 1: 10/12 rooms (83.4%); location 2: 8/9 (88.9%); location 3: 5/12 (50% as reported).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11834.intervention: Results disseminated to site managers with a recommendation to stock all rooms with tissues.

cycle2.result: Location 1 unchanged (83.4%); location 2 unchanged (88.9%); location 3 fell to 41%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2026.11834.other_findings: No trust policy existed; the authors conclude a more robust intervention and trust-wide policy guidance are needed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.584.standard: Mental Health Act Code of Practice, NICE standards and Trust seclusion policy (time of review, reason, diagnosis, MSE, physical health and observations, medication and side effects, risk, plan)

cycle1.result: Above 90% for time of review, record keeping, management plan, risk, MSE and physical health; prescribed medications 60%, medication side effects 40%, physical observations 40%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.584.intervention: Seclusion medical review template designed and incorporated into the existing documentation template, with teaching and training of doctors.

cycle2.result: Quality of seclusion medical review between 95% and 100%; no major concerns identified.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.584.other_findings: The project prompted nurses to audit nursing seclusion reviews.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.324.setting: Service for Adolescents and Families in Enfield, referrals from North Middlesex and Barnet hospital paediatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.324.standard: NICE Self-Harm Quality Standards (QS34): comprehensive psychosocial assessment, assessment within 24 hours if high risk, risk management plan and follow-up

cycle1.result: Comprehensive psychosocial assessment 100%; seen within 24 hours 93%; documented risk assessment 97%; 7-day follow-up review 92%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.324.intervention: Assessment protocol and safety plan, daily liaison with hospitals, paediatric nurses trained in the time to talk programme and a full-time crisis liaison nurse employed; re-audit planned.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.324.other_findings: Hospital referrals rose 141% from 2014/15 to 2018/19; 74% were girls and 87% presented with self-harm, suicidal ideation or attempt.

DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2025-327497.setting: 19 UK coronary sinus reducer implanting centres (national audit)
DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2025-327497.standard: Current guideline recommendations for CSR in refractory angina (appropriate patient selection)

cycle1.result: 84% had CCS class ≥3 angina despite ≥2 antianginals in 94%; baseline ischaemia testing 79%; procedural success 95%; periprocedural adverse events 9.2% (46 in 41 patients); 98% stayed ≤1 night.

DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2025-327497.other_findings: At 6 months 75% improved by ≥1 CCS class and 36% by ≥2 classes; MACE and severe adverse events <1%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.632.setting: Inpatient psychiatry department, tertiary care hospital, Faisalabad

cycle1.result: 27% criminal, 14.3% civil and 58.6% departmental cases; commonest diagnoses schizophrenia 27%, depression 23.5%, intellectual disability 18.9%; 14.9% had no psychiatric diagnosis.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.632.other_findings: Descriptive case review of referral sources and outcomes; 41.3% referred directly from courts.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.438.topic: Early intervention in psychosis waiting times
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.438.setting: Early Intervention in Psychosis service, Liverpool
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.438.standard: NICE access and waiting time standard: 60% of people with first episode psychosis treated with an approved care package within two weeks of referral

cycle1.result: Average referral-to-treatment pathway 9.8 days.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.438.intervention: Recommendations from the initial audit implemented (not detailed).

cycle2.result: Average pathway 22.5 days, above the NICE standard.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.438.other_findings: Main delays were referral assessment, care coordinator allocation and prescriber review; consultants did >50% of prescriber reviews in both periods. Worsening linked to COVID-19 and more referrals.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10596.setting: Three adult psychiatric inpatient wards (2 female, 1 male), Warneford Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10596.standard: Local Trust guidelines: all adult inpatients offered year-round vitamin D prophylaxis unless osteomalacia symptoms

cycle1.result: 8 (16%) prescribed prophylactic vitamin D; male ward 1 (6%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10596.intervention: Trust guidelines reformatted into a simplified poster and flow chart distributed to ward doctors' offices.

cycle2.result: 16 (31%) prescribed prophylactic vitamin D; male ward 5 (28%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10596.other_findings: Ward populations changed between measurements because of normal admissions and discharges.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10574.setting: Women's blended low/medium secure forensic psychiatry inpatient ward
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10574.standard: CRAMS criteria: 11 points on care plan, risk, activity, mental state and Section 17 leave in daily entries (adopted after CQC Mental Health Act Review)

cycle1.result: 814/1540 (52.9%) CRAMS criteria met: care planning 50.5%, risk 70.7%, activity 54.6%, mental state 49.8%, S17 leave 50.3%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10574.intervention: Findings discussed with the team, an information sheet produced and CRAMS discussed at daily team huddles.

cycle2.dates: One year after the initial cycle
cycle2.result: 1120/1540 (71.6%) met: care planning 72.6%, risk 75.0%, activity 70.7%, mental state 70.5%, S17 leave 70.7%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10574.other_findings: Many entries still did not meet full CRAMS criteria; an electronic template is planned with the new patient record system.

DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2017-311726.99.setting: Cardiac outpatient clinics, Barts Heart Centre

cycle1.result: Consultant utilisation of the SNOMED-based powerform averaged 60% for 327 new patients.

DOI:10.1136/heartjnl-2017-311726.99.other_findings: Structured summary reports were sent electronically to primary care the same day, replacing dictated letters; batch download of data worked.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10672.setting: Inpatient acute psychiatric ward and a rehabilitation centre
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10672.standard: 13 predefined PRN prescribing standards including generic naming, dose intervals, BNF limits and regular reviews

cycle1.result: Minimum dose interval 64.5%; maximum dose 96.7%; ward round reviews 3.2%; discontinuation of unused PRN 0%; review of regularly used PRN 0%; regular vs PRN use documented 33.3%.

cycle2.result: Minimum dose interval 93.5%; maximum dose 100%; ward round reviews 64.5%; discontinuation of unused PRN 22.2%; review of regularly used PRN 28.5%; regular vs PRN use documented 44.4%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10672.other_findings: Prompted by a serious incident. 100% compliance was sustained for generic naming, routes, BNF limits, indications and rewriting altered prescriptions.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.879.topic: Medication chart and consent to treatment documentation
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.879.setting: Acute mixed psychiatric inpatient unit, South Manchester (GMMH)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.879.standard: Local GMMH policy on medication chart documentation

cycle1.result: Capacity assessment form 22 (71%); consent to treatment form 16 (52%); depot route recorded 40%; regular administration date 84% and signature 29%; allergy reaction nature 6/21 (29%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.879.intervention: Planned: recommendations and re-audit in 3–6 months.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.879.other_findings: PRN administration details were 100% complete; patient identifiers were not maintained throughout the chart.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.501.topic: Admission blood tests on psychiatric wards
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.501.setting: Norbury House PICU, St George's Hospital, Stafford, Midlands Partnership NHS Foundation Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.501.standard: MPFT trust guidelines on routine admission blood tests

cycle1.result: TFTs 71%; glucose 6%; prolactin 77%; calcium 94%; unnecessary tests in 88% of patients (23 tests).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.501.intervention: Staff education programme on trust admission blood test guidelines.

cycle2.result: Appropriate admission bloods 69%; TFTs 100%; glucose 69%; prolactin 100%; calcium 92%; unnecessary tests in 21% (3 tests).

cycle1.result: 5193 (3.2%) had predicted mortality ≥50%; 90-day survival 43% (50–59%), 34% (60–69%), 27% (70–79%) and 17% (80+); unplanned return to theatre 11% vs 8% in high-risk patients.

DOI:10.1111/anae.16130.other_findings: Median length of stay rose from 26 days (group 50–59) to 35 days (group 80+) versus 17 days for high-risk patients.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.210.standard: NICE guidelines: assessment of biological symptoms and discussion of treatment side effects before initiation and at follow-up

cycle1.result: No record of sexual dysfunction as present or absent at initial assessment or follow-up (0%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.210.intervention: Suggested training and recording changes; proposed standard that recording absence of biological symptoms or supplying medicine leaflets is adequate.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.210.other_findings: A staff survey showed high confidence and high self-reported discussion of sexual dysfunction despite no documentation.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.575.topic: Driving safety discussion in mental health
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.575.setting: Kingston and Richmond Home Treatment Teams, South West London and St George's NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.575.standard: DVLA advice on driving and notification during changes in mental health condition

cycle1.result: 17.7% had documented driving discussion.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.575.intervention: Findings presented at Trust-wide HTT governance meeting; driving prompt added to the initial assessment proforma and DVLA leaflet added to the welcome pack.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.575.other_findings: Three cycles: an interim re-audit at two months showed 33.3%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.498.setting: Three adolescent forensic wards (2 medium secure, 1 low secure), FCAMHS Ardenleigh, Birmingham
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.498.standard: National Chlamydia Screening Programme: screening of at-risk young people

cycle1.result: 11.5% tested for chlamydia while 36.8% met screening criteria; physical health (Rethink) form completed in 73.7%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.498.intervention: Recommendations from the initial audit (not detailed).
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.498.other_findings: Physical health forms were no longer in use by the re-audit; including chlamydia screening in admission processes is suggested.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.104.setting: One community Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service team
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.104.standard: Licensed use per Summary of Product Characteristics and NICE, BAP and BNFc guidance

cycle1.result: 177 prescriptions: 25% licensed use; 42% NICE-compatible, 62% BAP-compatible, 67% BNFc-compatible; 12% deviated from all guidance.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2023.104.other_findings: Unsupported prescriptions included melatonin (9), quetiapine (6) and olanzapine (4) and were linked to comorbidity; 88% were supported by licence or guidance.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10589.topic: STOMP psychotropic review in learning disability
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10589.setting: Four adult learning disability teams, Tees, Esk and Wear Valleys NHS Trust
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10589.standard: NICE NG11: documented rationale, likely treatment length and written strategy for reviewing and stopping psychotropics shared with non-specialists

cycle1.result: Rationale documented 102 (92.7%); review strategy 44 (40%); timescale for stopping 32 (29%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10589.intervention: Planned: STOMP awareness, STOMP team involvement, discharge template prompts for review/stop timescale and STOMP pathway GP guidance; re-audit in 6 months.
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10589.other_findings: 81 patients were prescribed medication for other mental health diagnoses rather than challenging behaviour.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.549.setting: Six adult inpatient wards, St Charles Hospital
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.549.standard: 10 items agreed with community psychiatric colleagues (reason for admission, diagnosis, circumstances, progress, risk, physical health, legal status, medication, plan, contact details)

cycle1.result: 3.3% (1/30) complete for all items; 23.3% (7/30) missing one item; 7/30 had no information; reason for admission recorded in 2/30.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.549.other_findings: Four empty summaries were written in progress notes rather than the proforma; reason for admission was often recorded unhelpfully as "in crisis".

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.561.setting: Three psychiatric units (Heddfan, Ablett, Hergest) and CMHT sites, Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.561.standard: NICE NG53 and CCQI Standards for Community-Based Mental Health Services 2017: 72-hour follow-up with MSE and comprehensive care plan

cycle1.result: 23% did not receive 72-hour follow-up; risk assessment documented 74%; MSE at follow-up 87%; 67% met full follow-up documentation criteria.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.561.other_findings: Thorough inpatient assessments in 83%; printouts from the electronic discharge system were often unavailable.

cycle1.result: 72% (n = 26) much better or better on PGA; DLQI reduction in 28% (n = 10); no complications in 94% (n = 34); minor burn in 6% (n = 2).

DOI:10.1093/bjd/ljae090.177.other_findings: Prospective cohort of treatment outcomes, not measured against a standard.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac276.setting: Australian and New Zealand Audit of Surgical Mortality (national database)

cycle1.result: 67 deaths; estimated mortality 0.03–0.07 per cent; 27 (40 per cent) precipitated by significant adverse events; 18 (27 per cent) judged preventable.

DOI:10.1093/bjs/znac276.other_findings: Themes: inadequate preoperative assessment, unanticipated intraoperative pitfalls and failure to recognise postoperative complications.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.281.setting: Child and Adolescent Mental Health Service, Massereene House, Northern Health and Social Care Trust

cycle1.result: 80% rated the help received "a great deal" better and 80% would recommend telephone reviews "a great deal".

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2021.281.other_findings: Satisfaction questionnaire; some preferred face-to-face reviews and the reviewing doctor also ran the audit, risking bias.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10634.standard: NICE: all CAMHS inpatients offered maintenance vitamin D supplementation from November to March

cycle1.result: 1 out of 10 inpatients received vitamin D supplementation; 5 had levels checked in past three months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10634.intervention: 1:1 psychoeducation from a doctor and a clinic room poster promoting opportunistic vitamin D testing and supplementation.

cycle2.result: 9 out of 10 prescribed vitamin D (7 prophylaxis, 2 treatment doses); 5 had levels checked in past three months.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10634.other_findings: Three cycles: 9 out of 11 prescribed on 06/01/2025. Vitamin D level monitoring did not improve.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.499.setting: Five chronic psychiatric inpatient wards, Mount Carmel Hospital, compared with Saint Vincent De Paule Residence

cycle1.result: Resuscitation form completion 73.47% (MCH) vs 94.90% (SVPR); "Not for CPR" 9.72% (MCH) vs 61.29% (SVPR).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2022.499.other_findings: SVPR patients had more comorbidities (3.50 vs 2.47, p = 0.0002) with similar frailty (5.83 vs 5.48, p = 0.1456). Resuscitation training tailored to psychiatry was introduced.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.589.topic: GP registration and medical card status in addiction care plans
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.589.setting: National Drug Treatment Centre, Dublin (addiction psychiatry)
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.589.standard: HSE Clinical Guidelines for Opiate Substitution Therapy 2016: care plan based on assessed need for all drug users in treatment

cycle1.result: GP registration on care plan 66%; up-to-date medical card 12%; medical card status unknown 72%; medical card number displayed 25%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.589.intervention: Results discussed at MDT; staff discussed medical card and GP status at every interaction and referred patients to social work for applications and GP registration.

cycle2.result: GP registration on care plan 93%; up-to-date medical card 45%; status unknown 44%; medical card number displayed 55%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2024.589.other_findings: Still short of 100% compliance; action plan developed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10644.topic: Cancer screening discussion on psychiatric admission
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10644.setting: Acute adult psychiatric wards (Galleywood, Topaz), Mother and Baby Unit (Rainbow) and PICU (Christopher Unit)

cycle1.result: Cervical screening discussed with 4/43 eligible (9%); breast screening discussed with 1/15 eligible (7%).

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10644.intervention: Enhanced induction teaching for resident doctors and local academic teaching over 9 months.

cycle2.result: Cervical screening discussed with 5/26 (19%); breast screening with 0/5 eligible.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10644.other_findings: Doctors cited lack of time, patients unable to answer and perceived irrelevance; further teaching and reminder posters followed.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10654.setting: Stanley Ward, 30-bed acute male psychiatric ward, Wakefield
DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10654.standard: RCPsych CCQI Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services: documentation of capacity, physical health, medications and leave

cycle1.result: Fully documented: capacity 35%, physical health 0%, medications 22%, leave 20%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10654.intervention: Inpatient list for ward doctors with each domain to copy into MDT notes, then an interactive training video of a simulated MDT shown at departmental teaching.

cycle2.result: Fully documented: capacity 45%, physical health 42%, medications 68%, leave 77%.

DOI:10.1192/bjo.2025.10654.other_findings: Four measurements: late March 2024 capacity 59%, physical 41%, medications 82%, leave 68% full; July 2024 capacity 20%, physical 48%, medications 91%, leave 71% full. Trainee rotation and limited meeting time hindered sustained gains.
